capability.description: Accepted product behavior is strict, reviewable, and measurable beside the implementation.
capability.name: Living product contract

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Tieline must reject repository contract documents that violate the accepted Story and Acceptance Criterion schema.
acceptance_criteria.rationale: Structural failures make semantic impact and synchronization untrustworthy.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Repository sync must record each Story, acceptance criterion, and screen a synced commit's history added, changed, or removed, with its commit and pull request, backfilling from git history on its first record and recording only what changed after the last recorded commit afterwards, must record nothing twice, must leave sync unchanged when the synced commit is not a git commit, and exact acceptance criterion context must include the criterion's changes.
acceptance_criteria.rationale: Agents and hosted readers without a checkout need to know when and in which pull request behavior last changed, and a sync that runs again or late must neither duplicate nor lose that history.

scenarios.given: two pull requests merged between two syncs
scenarios.then: each change must be recorded with the pull request that made it

scenarios.given: a clone that cannot read some commits in the synced history, such as a partial clone
scenarios.then: it must not record changes newer than those commits, so a later sync that can read them records the gap and what followed it

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Tieline must compile deterministic manifests and report direct-AC and repository mapping coverage with explicit gaps.

scenarios.given: ten eligible source files and eight mapped paths
scenarios.then: Tieline must report 80 percent coverage and name both unmapped files

scenarios.given: configured source roots contain no eligible files
scenarios.then: Tieline must report that coverage is not measured instead of reporting 100 percent

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Tieline must report affected Acceptance Criteria and freshness for changed, renamed, or deleted linked paths without blocking on semantic findings.
acceptance_criteria.rationale: Drift should be visible during review while the MVP remains warn-only.

scenarios.given: a linked implementation path changes without a refreshed manifest
scenarios.then: Tieline must report the linked criterion as impacted and stale
scenarios.when: the branch is checked against its base

scenarios.given: the base branch gained commits after the branch was created
scenarios.then: Tieline must compare from the branch point and report only the branch's own changes
scenarios.when: the branch is checked against that base

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Tieline must render accepted Stories and Acceptance Criteria as a self-contained human-readable review page.
acceptance_criteria.rationale: Maintainers outside the implementation can review the same repository-owned contract accepted by the pull request.

scenarios.given: a repository whose contract has no capabilities yet
scenarios.then: the page must say there are no capabilities yet and how to begin onboarding with the installed skill

scenarios.given: a contract that does not validate
scenarios.then: the page must list the validation notes and say the contract does not validate, without offering onboarding

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Tieline must store the compiled manifest as one file per capability beside a repository-level index, must delete the file of any capability the contract no longer declares, and must refuse to read a manifest whose file names disagree with the capabilities they hold.
acceptance_criteria.rationale: A single generated manifest made every branch that touched any specification file conflict with every other one, even when the capabilities they changed were disjoint, and let a partial line merge produce a manifest that parses but that no compilation would emit.

scenarios.given: a compiled manifest whose capability was removed from the specification
scenarios.then: Tieline must delete that capability's manifest file and leave every other file in the manifest directory untouched

scenarios.given: a manifest file whose name does not match the capability it holds
scenarios.then: Tieline must refuse the manifest and name both the file and the capability instead of accepting the capability under the wrong identity

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Tieline must fail the check when the committed manifest differs from the manifest the contract compiles to, unless that gate is explicitly downgraded.
acceptance_criteria.rationale: A manifest merged without recompilation records evidence hashes that were never reviewed against the code they name. Comparing the committed manifest with a fresh compilation is a byte diff of a deterministic function, so nothing is being judged, which is the same reason broken links already fail. Findings that do need judgement stay warn-only.

scenarios.given: a specification file changed without the manifest being recompiled
scenarios.then: Tieline must report the stale manifest as an error and exit non-zero
scenarios.when: the branch is checked against its base

scenarios.given: the same stale manifest and an explicit request to downgrade the gate
scenarios.then: Tieline must report the stale manifest as a warning and exit zero
scenarios.when: the branch is checked against its base

scenarios.given: a manifest that cannot be recompiled at all
scenarios.then: Tieline must report the compilation failure once rather than also reporting it as a stale manifest
scenarios.when: the branch is checked against its base

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Tieline must require every contract link to state whether its claim was authored, inferred, or materialized, and must preserve that provenance through compiled manifests, repository synchronization, and every exact claim read.
acceptance_criteria.rationale: Relation and target describe what a link claims, while provenance records how that claim entered its current authority surface. Keeping this low-cardinality origin distinct from freshness and grade lets agents interpret a claim without turning mutable review facts into contract identity.

scenarios.given: a contract link has no provenance
scenarios.then: Tieline must reject the link instead of guessing where its claim came from

scenarios.given: only a contract link's provenance changes
scenarios.then: Tieline must change the owning contract hash without creating a second link identity

scenarios.given: an accepted repository link was copied during planning-to-repository authority transfer
scenarios.then: Tieline must preserve materialized as the origin of that exact claim
scenarios.when: the repository contract is synchronized and read

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Tieline must keep the compiled manifest independent of Git revision, identify exact manifest reads with a content-derived digest, and supply Git commit provenance explicitly only when synchronizing the reviewed manifest to the database.
acceptance_criteria.rationale: A revision in the tracked repository-level index made every branch conflict in one shared generated file and became stale as soon as that generated file was committed. Content identity belongs to the reviewed manifest, while Git revision belongs to the runtime projection checkpoint and audit boundary.

scenarios.given: accepted specifications and linked artifacts whose content is unchanged across two Git revisions
scenarios.then: the repository-level manifest index must remain byte-identical and must not record either Git revision
scenarios.when: the contract is compiled at each revision

scenarios.given: the content of the reviewed manifest changes
scenarios.then: Tieline must return a different manifest digest identifying the complete reviewed manifest that answered

scenarios.given: a reviewed manifest and an explicit runtime Git commit
scenarios.then: Tieline must use that runtime commit for projection rows, checkpoint guards, sync results, and audit events without adding it to the reviewed manifest

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Tieline must report, from git alone, when each Story, acceptance criterion, and screen was added, changed, or removed and in which pull request, by comparing each first-parent commit's compiled manifest with its parent's, must show each one's last change on the review page, and must say when older history was not read or a commit's manifest is not held by the clone instead of attributing changes it cannot see.
acceptance_criteria.rationale: Reviewers and agents need to know which change last touched a piece of behavior, and a shallow or partial clone must not make every item look newly added.

scenarios.given: a pull request merged with a merge commit changed an acceptance criterion on its branch
scenarios.then: the change must be attributed to the merge commit and its pull request
scenarios.when: the history of main is read

scenarios.given: a long history whose manifest file listings together exceed the history's bound, though each fits alone
scenarios.then: Tieline must fail and name the bound rather than hold every commit's listing

stories.benefit: intent and implementation change through the same review
stories.goal: define product behavior in a stable Story and Acceptance Criterion hierarchy
stories.title: Review accepted behavior with code

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Tieline must report every acceptance criterion linked to an exact repository-relative path, must distinguish a link carried by the acceptance criterion itself from one carried only by its Story, and must return an explicit has_criteria, no_criteria, or not_found status for every requested path.
acceptance_criteria.rationale: Coverage answers for the whole contract and check answers for a diff, so both describe a violation that already exists; the pre-change question is the only one that can prevent it. An empty array reads to an agent like a failed query rather than the actionable finding that an existing path has no recorded acceptance criteria.

scenarios.given: a path is linked by one acceptance criterion and by the Story that owns it
scenarios.then: Tieline must return has_criteria with both records marked direct and story_fallback
scenarios.when: the contract criteria for that path are requested

scenarios.given: a path exists in the repository and no contract link targets it
scenarios.then: Tieline must return no_criteria and state that no acceptance criteria apply instead of returning an empty result
scenarios.when: the contract criteria for that path are requested

scenarios.given: a requested path does not exist in the repository
scenarios.then: Tieline must return not_found distinctly from an existing path with no criteria
scenarios.when: the contract criteria for that path are requested

acceptance_criteria.criterion: The path-criteria lookup must answer from the compiled manifest alone, so Tieline must serve get_path_criteria over MCP with no database connection and must return a named, actionable message when no workspace or no readable manifest is found.
acceptance_criteria.rationale: Every other MCP tool fails at call time without Postgres, so an offline server boots and answers nothing; a manifest-backed lookup is what makes serving without a database worth doing, and an obscure throw would waste the one answer the caller came for.

scenarios.given: no database connection is configured
scenarios.then: Tieline must return the applicable acceptance criteria and the content-derived digest of the manifest that answered
scenarios.when: the contract criteria for a path are requested over MCP

scenarios.given: the server runs outside any Tieline workspace
scenarios.then: Tieline must name the missing workspace and the command that creates one
scenarios.when: the contract criteria for a path are requested

aliases: which acceptance criteria apply to this file
stories.benefit: a contradiction with accepted behavior is prevented instead of reported afterwards
stories.goal: resolve a repository path to the acceptance criteria already recorded for it
stories.title: Learn which acceptance criteria apply to a path before editing it

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Given an exact repository-relative code or test path with optional kind and selector, Tieline must preserve the complete locator identity, return has_context, no_criteria, or not_found explicitly, include exact-selector and file-level claims while excluding other selectors, and bound associated assets to one Acceptance-Criterion-mediated intent neighborhood.
acceptance_criteria.rationale: A known symbol should retrieve the reviewed behavior that applies to that symbol without collapsing same-file claims or pretending the result is an open-ended graph traversal.

scenarios.given: one file has claims for function:first, function:second, and the whole file
scenarios.then: Tieline must return the function:first and file-level claims with their kind, repository, canonical path, selector, framework hint, relation, provenance, and link scope while excluding function:second
scenarios.when: exact asset context is requested for function:first

scenarios.given: an existing path has no applicable claim for the requested selector
scenarios.then: Tieline must return no_criteria distinctly from not_found for a missing path

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Given an exact Acceptance Criterion stable ID, Tieline must return its Capability and Story ancestry, lifecycle, criterion, rationale, applicability, scenarios, direct links, Story-fallback links, and directly associated code and test assets without recursive code-to-code traversal.
acceptance_criteria.rationale: Reviewers need the accepted product record and its bounded contract coupling, not a semantic approximation or an inferred runtime dependency graph.

scenarios.given: an Acceptance Criterion has a direct test link and inherits a Story-level implementation link
scenarios.then: Tieline must preserve both assets, their direct or story_fallback scope, and the owning product context in deterministic order

scenarios.given: the stable ID does not identify an accepted Acceptance Criterion
scenarios.then: Tieline must return an explicit not_found status and an actionable answer naming the unknown stable ID and reviewed manifest

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Every code or test claim returned as exact intent context must keep provenance, link scope, content freshness, locator resolution, and semantic support as separate assurance dimensions, must preserve broken and uninspectable claims with honest causes or unknown states, and must report semantic support as not_assessed.
acceptance_criteria.rationale: Structural currency and selector resolution can guide review, but neither proves the linked behavior or records that a linked test executed or passed.

scenarios.given: a current local implementation selector resolves against its reviewed content
scenarios.then: provenance, freshness, and locator resolution must be positive while semantic support remains not_assessed

scenarios.given: a local target is missing or a selector uses an unsupported language
scenarios.then: the claim must remain visible with a named broken cause or not_checked state and must not be converted into semantic failure

scenarios.given: an associated target names another repository
scenarios.then: freshness and locator resolution must remain honestly unknown or not_checked
scenarios.when: its claim is inspected from this checkout

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Tieline must expose separate get_asset_intent_context and get_acceptance_criterion_context MCP tools and equivalent contract context --path and --ac CLI modes that answer from the compiled manifest without a database and preserve the same membership, statuses, repository key, and content-derived manifest digest.
acceptance_criteria.rationale: Agents need primitive exact reads while maintainers need CLI and JSON parity to inspect the same reviewed contract and actionable workspace or manifest failures.

scenarios.given: no database, embeddings, network, or knowledge store is configured and the compiled manifest is readable
scenarios.then: both surfaces must return the same bounded neighborhood membership and manifest identity
scenarios.when: equivalent exact context requests are made over MCP and CLI

scenarios.given: no workspace or no readable manifest is available
scenarios.then: Tieline must return a named actionable result that explains how to initialize or compile the workspace
scenarios.when: either MCP exact context tool is called

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Diff impact must preserve selector-qualified target identity and report resolved, unresolved, or not_checked locator state for affected links while keeping selector findings advisory and describing shared Acceptance-Criterion links only as contract coupling rather than runtime dependency or comprehensive blast radius.
acceptance_criteria.rationale: Selector drift is useful review input, but conservative inspection cannot establish execution topology and must not create a new blocking gate.

scenarios.given: a changed file contains one unresolved selector claim and one selector in an unsupported source language
scenarios.then: both claims must remain distinct with unresolved and not_checked locator states and selector findings must not change the existing exit behavior

stories.benefit: implementation and review begin from bounded accepted intent with honest current assurance
stories.goal: retrieve the exact reviewed context for a known code or test locator or Acceptance Criterion
stories.title: Inspect precise accepted intent before changing an asset

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Tieline must extract deterministic symbols, owner chains where applicable, named UTF-16 and UTF-8 byte source ranges, and parser-backed source snippets from immutable JavaScript, JSX, TypeScript, TSX, Python, Rust, and SQL snapshots while retaining syntax recovery, ambiguity, and truncation explicitly; it must also extract module references only for languages with a supported static module model.
acceptance_criteria.rationale: Structural evidence is useful only when callers can identify the exact bytes and parser compatibility that produced it without treating a best-effort parse as semantic proof.

scenarios.given: supported source contains nested declarations, Unicode names, imports, and a recoverable syntax error
scenarios.then: facts must preserve canonical selectors, complete owners, both coordinate systems, syntax status, diagnostics, and deterministic compatibility identity

scenarios.given: a reviewed selector resolves uniquely against hash-current source
scenarios.then: a bounded parser-backed snippet may be returned while semantic support remains not_assessed

scenarios.given: SQL declares a top-level table, view, or function with a safely representable name
scenarios.then: Tieline must expose its declaration selector and ranges without claiming SQL dependency edges

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Tieline must resolve supported project-local JavaScript and TypeScript, Python, and Rust module forms in a separate conservative phase and must preserve exact, ambiguous, unresolved, external, dynamic, glob, generated, and unsupported outcomes instead of guessing a dependency.
acceptance_criteria.rationale: A false edge produces a misleading blast radius, while an explicit frontier gives an agent a precise place to continue investigation.

scenarios.given: a static local import has one inventory-backed target
scenarios.then: Tieline must record its rule, target, configuration identity, and derived edge

scenarios.given: a dynamic name, glob, generated module, unsupported configuration, external package, or multiple target is encountered
scenarios.then: Tieline must retain a named non-resolved outcome and candidates or diagnostics without manufacturing an exact edge

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Tieline must identify topology generations from selected source and resolver inputs plus parser, resolver, schema, and fact-policy compatibility, must publish one deterministic bounded repository graph.json only through explicit compilation, and must publish hosted relational generations only when complete.
acceptance_criteria.rationale: Readers must never observe a mixed or partial graph, generated artifact bytes must not make identity self-referential, and reviewed repository topology must remain distinct from richer hosted persistence.

scenarios.given: topology compilation is interrupted or loses a concurrent publication race
scenarios.then: readers must observe either the previous complete graph.json or the complete winning graph.json and never a partial document

scenarios.given: files change while a working-tree generation is built
scenarios.then: Tieline must return workspace_changed without publishing mixed facts
scenarios.when: the consistency check retries and observes another change

scenarios.given: only generated topology bytes or unrelated authored intent change
scenarios.then: the selected-input identity must remain unchanged
scenarios.when: topology identity and artifact bytes are recomputed

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Tieline must locate an exact path and optional selector before traversing dependencies or dependents, must default AC-aware blast radius to dependents, and must return cycle-safe deterministic paths, unresolved frontiers, generation identities, and independent depth, node, edge, and path truncation within fixed hard maxima.
acceptance_criteria.rationale: Bounded topology is safe for agent use only when ambiguity and omitted work stay visible and the caller cannot bypass product limits.

scenarios.given: a dependency graph contains a cycle, diamond, ambiguous start, and unresolved reference
scenarios.then: Tieline must preserve all applicable start and frontier outcomes without revisiting nodes indefinitely

scenarios.given: a changed locator and another unrelated locator share one Acceptance Criterion
scenarios.then: the unrelated locator must not be traversed unless a derived code edge reaches it

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Tieline must expose equivalent read-only CLI and MCP artifact-backed dependency-trace and AC-aware blast-radius results, must join base and current code to their matching authored manifest roles, must label code edges as derived_code_dependency and authored joins as contract_coupling with may_be_impacted and semantic_support not_assessed, and must never infer implementation satisfaction or a code dependency from a shared Acceptance Criterion.
acceptance_criteria.rationale: Derived topology can prioritize investigation and preserve deleted-side intent, but accepted YAML and its compiled manifest remain the authority for business intent and normal review remains the acceptance boundary.

scenarios.given: a local workspace has no database connection
scenarios.then: both surfaces must select the existing current repository artifact without parsing or writing and return equivalent structured membership
scenarios.when: dependency trace or AC-aware blast radius is requested

scenarios.given: a base commit removes linked code or the current manifest removes its authored claim
scenarios.then: each visited locator must join only to its matching manifest role while unclaimed locators remain visible
scenarios.when: AC-aware blast radius compares base and current

scenarios.given: hosted mode has a compatible complete topology generation but no readable authored manifest
scenarios.then: dependency trace may run while AC-aware contract joining must report contract_unavailable

stories.benefit: code changes can be investigated with bounded structural evidence while reviewed product intent remains authoritative
stories.goal: trace conservative multi-language code relationships and their potentially affected accepted intent
stories.title: Inspect derived code topology without weakening contract authority

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Tieline must leave compile, check, review, sync, and exact context reads unchanged and must never read a screen catalog unless the repository enables screens in its configuration.
acceptance_criteria.rationale: Screens are optional; a repository that does not opt in must not pay for or be broken by the feature.

scenarios.given: a repository without an enabled screens block contains a screen catalog directory
scenarios.then: every output must be byte-identical to the same repository without the directory
scenarios.when: the contract is validated, compiled, reviewed, and checked

scenarios.given: a repository that has not enabled screens authors a shows link
scenarios.then: Tieline must reject the link and say how to opt in

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Tieline must account for every catalogued screen as captured or marked not captured with one of a closed set of reasons, must skip marked screens and report selected screens no test tags instead of failing the capture, must report page files no screen claims and acceptance criteria showing screens that no @ac-tagged test linked from them proves, must keep screens that differ between repeated captures out of the committed outputs, and must fail a strict audit while any of these remain.
acceptance_criteria.rationale: Captures are only worth reviewing if every screen a user can reach is either captured from the real app or explicitly excused, and documented UI behavior is proven by a test, so gaps must be visible and gateable rather than silently skipped.

scenarios.given: a screen needs a faked response to be reached
scenarios.then: capture must skip it and the audit must list it with its reason as accounted for
scenarios.when: it is marked not captured with reason needs-real-trigger

scenarios.given: a branch adds a page file that no screen's paths claim
scenarios.then: Tieline must warn about the new page file without changing the exit code

acceptance_criteria.criterion: The Tieline skill must have agents capture screens only from the real app and mark a state they cannot reach without a faked response as not captured, write the scene for a screen an acceptance criterion shows as that criterion's tagged and linked test asserting its Then, backfill from acceptance criteria before other states while reporting states no criterion describes, offer screen capture during onboarding of a repository with a user interface and backfill before reporting when the user accepts, and keep a screens-enabled repository's captures current before handing off a change to what users see.
acceptance_criteria.rationale: Most scenes are written by agents, so the skill decides whether captures are truthful, whether documented behavior is proven, and whether a catalog stays complete as the product changes.

scenarios.given: onboarding a web app whose user accepts screen capture, with a provisioned or existing database
scenarios.then: it must also offer hosted screens, and must not offer them for an offline or local database

scenarios.given: onboarding enabled screens
scenarios.then: the onboarding pull request must add the screens check workflow the skill ships, or the hosted workflows in its place when hosted screens were accepted

acceptance_criteria.criterion: With hosted screens enabled, Tieline must publish a pull request's or branch's review page, compared with main's published state and showing a changed screen's previous image, only after every image the page shows is in the object store, must upload only images whose bytes match their catalog digest and are PNG, JPEG, WebP, GIF, or AVIF, must replace that ref's previous page, and must publish main's page only from repository sync and only for the commit sync last recorded.
acceptance_criteria.rationale: A hosted page is reviewed as evidence of a change, so it must never show an image the store lacks or one the catalog does not record, and publishing a pull request must never change what main shows.

scenarios.given: a screenshot a page shows is neither in the object store nor usable in the captures directory
scenarios.then: Tieline must name the screen and publish nothing

scenarios.given: the capture publisher's database credentials
scenarios.then: the database must refuse
scenarios.when: they are used to write main's page or history, or to delete anything

scenarios.given: a sync of an older commit finishes after a sync of a newer one
scenarios.then: Tieline must keep the newer page

scenarios.given: the bucket holds an image's key with other bytes, and the captures directory holds the bytes the catalog names
scenarios.then: Tieline must store the image again before publishing the page, rather than count it as already stored

scenarios.given: a pull request's page shows main's image beside a screen whose image it changed
scenarios.then: main's image must stay stored while the pull request's page shows it
scenarios.when: main later replaces that screen's image more times than retention keeps

scenarios.given: the example pull-request workflow, and a pull request whose dependencies or tests are compromised
scenarios.then: the publishing credentials must be held only by a workflow the default branch owns, in an environment only the default branch can use, that installs Tieline from the default branch and runs none of the pull request's code

scenarios.given: the bucket holds an image the database has no record of, as after restoring the database apart from its bucket, and the captures directory cannot supply it
scenarios.then: Tieline must publish nothing and name the image, since the site would not serve it
scenarios.when: a page that shows it is published

scenarios.given: a trusted checkout, and a pull request whose configuration names another repository key, bucket, or site URL
scenarios.then: Tieline must publish nothing and touch neither the database nor the bucket
scenarios.when: the pull request is published with --trusted

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Tieline must delete a closed pull request's hosted page only after a grace period, a branch's page after the configured days without a publish, and main's image history beyond the configured number of replaced images per screen, and must delete an image only when no page or retained history references it and nothing referenced it within a grace period, removing it from the object store before its record and keeping the record of any image it could not remove.
acceptance_criteria.rationale: Hosted screens must stay bounded without deleting an image a page still shows, a merge is about to make main show, or a publish has just claimed.

scenarios.given: the object store refuses to delete one of two unreferenced images
scenarios.then: Tieline must delete the other image and its record, and keep the refused image's record so the next run retries it

scenarios.given: a screen main's page no longer shows
scenarios.then: its history must be deleted, so its images can go once nothing else references them; when main's page cannot be read, history is kept and the prune says why

scenarios.given: object storage stalls while a prune deletes unreferenced images
scenarios.then: it must stop deleting at its time limit and release the screens lock, keeping what it did not delete for the next prune

acceptance_criteria.criterion: The hosted screens site must serve only pages publishing stored, by ref with main by default, and only images a publish recorded whose bytes still match their digest, must send every response marked as the site's with nosniff, no framing, and no shared caching, must answer an unpublished or malformed ref, an unknown path, or another method without reading the object store, and must hand an image larger than the host can return to a presigned link that expires within a minute.
acceptance_criteria.rationale: The site exposes review evidence over the network behind only the host's access control, so it must never serve anything publishing did not record, nor bytes that changed after they were verified.

scenarios.given: the site is deployed without its database or object storage settings, or with an invalid repository key
scenarios.then: the site must answer as itself with an error naming what is missing or invalid, instead of failing to load

scenarios.given: an object in the bucket was overwritten after its image was published
scenarios.then: the site must refuse it rather than serve the new bytes

scenarios.given: a published image too large for the host to return whose bytes in the bucket were replaced
scenarios.then: the site must refuse it instead of redirecting to the bucket

scenarios.given: a catalog image given by an http URL
scenarios.then: the page must show the screen without a picture rather than a broken image
scenarios.when: its screen is shown on a hosted page, which allows only https images

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Tieline must write a site for a supported host without replacing edited files unless forced or writing outside the repository, and tieline hosted check must write, find, and delete a probe object in the bucket, must confirm that each database credential set can do its job and that the site's credential cannot write, and must fail when the deployed site answers a visitor who has not logged in.
acceptance_criteria.rationale: Hosted screens depend on a bucket, three database credentials, and the host's access control being right, and a team must be able to prove all of them before trusting the site with its review evidence.

scenarios.given: the host's access control protects static files but not the site's functions
scenarios.then: Tieline must fail because the site answered a visitor who had not logged in
scenarios.when: tieline hosted check runs against the site

scenarios.given: the publishing credential is the sync role, an owner, or another role that can delete, write history, rewrite a page's ref or an image's record, or escape row security
scenarios.then: Tieline must fail and name what a capture job must not hold, as it must for a role that lacks what publishing needs

scenarios.given: the site redirects an anonymous visitor to another host or page that serves the site
scenarios.then: Tieline must follow at most a bounded number of redirects and fail, passing only on a 401 or 403 or a redirect to a login

scenarios.given: a check fails after the storage probe was written
scenarios.then: the probe object must still be deleted

scenarios.given: a symbolic link inside the site directory where a site file or directory goes
scenarios.then: Tieline must refuse without writing through the link
scenarios.when: tieline hosted init runs, even with --force

scenarios.given: the sync credential is the capture publisher's, or another role row security keeps off main's page
scenarios.then: Tieline must fail and name what sync needs that the role lacks

scenarios.given: the site's credential can write any table, even only update or delete published screens, or write on one column only
scenarios.then: Tieline must fail, because the site's credential must only read

scenarios.given: the site URL has a path, such as https://screens.example.test/screens
scenarios.then: Tieline must ask for the page and an image beneath that path, not at the origin's root
scenarios.when: tieline hosted check runs against the site

scenarios.given: the site's or the publishing credential holds its role's grants, copied by hand, without membership in the role row security names
scenarios.then: Tieline must fail, because row security would hide published pages from it or let it write none

scenarios.given: the publishing credential can also write contract change events, or any table beyond the pages and images it publishes
scenarios.then: Tieline must fail and name each write a capture job must not hold

acceptance_criteria.criterion: The Tieline skill must have agents provision hosted screens storage in a region with object storage, with a read-write credential for publishing and a read-only one for the hosted site, written straight to private files outside the repository, must never have them print a secret, read one back, or ask the user to paste one, and must have them verify the bucket, the database credentials, and the site's access control with tieline hosted check.
acceptance_criteria.rationale: Provisioning is done by agents holding the user's provider account, so the skill decides whether storage credentials stay least-privilege and out of transcripts.

scenarios.given: onboarding provisions a hosted database
scenarios.then: it must be created in a region with object storage, aws-us-east-2 unless the user named another, without asking the user for a region

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Tieline must generate, as one committed scene file, a scene for every catalogued page that no other test captures and that is not marked not captured, each running the repository's setup module before opening the page, must skip and report a route with parameters when no setup module chooses its URL, must fail a generated scene whose page answers with an error or whose route keeps a parameter, and must fail the strict audit while the generated file differs from what the catalog generates.
acceptance_criteria.rationale: Scenes are written by agents, not people, so every page must be captured without anyone writing a test just to open it, and a stale or wrong generated scene must never stand in for the screen.

scenarios.given: an agent writes its own scene for a page that has a generated scene
scenarios.then: the page must leave the generated file so it is captured once

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Tieline must reject screen catalog entries with unknown kinds or fields, reserved phase-two fields, duplicate keys, unknown capabilities, unsafe image locators, or values beyond their bounds, and must reject shows links to screens the catalog does not contain.
acceptance_criteria.rationale: The catalog is the reference a shows link resolves against, so an invalid entry or an unresolvable key would make screen review untrustworthy.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Tieline must compile the screen catalog and shows links into the manifest deterministically without changing any contract hash, must fail check on an invalid catalog or a committed shows link to a removed screen, and must remove screens before database sync.
acceptance_criteria.rationale: The manifest is the reviewed read model, so screens must appear in it reproducibly, while the database and evidence consumers keep seeing exactly the contract they saw before screens existed.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: The screen importer must bound and validate untrusted JSON before writing, must update catalog entries by key so a repeated import changes nothing, must delete entries only when pruning is requested, and must refuse or explicitly skip entries for undeclared capabilities.
acceptance_criteria.rationale: Most catalog entries arrive from external capture tools, so the importer is a trust boundary and must be safe to run repeatedly.

scenarios.given: an import names a capability the contract does not declare
scenarios.then: Tieline must name the unknown capability and write nothing
scenarios.when: the import runs without the skip option

scenarios.given: an import changes the screenshot of a screen Tieline captured
scenarios.then: Tieline must drop the screen's capture record, keep it when the picture is unchanged, and refuse capture records in the input

acceptance_criteria.criterion: The review page must show every catalogued screen grouped by capability and group with kind, applicability, and link filters, search, a detail panel, coverage counts, and each Story's and AC's linked screens, and must render placeholders when screenshots are missing.
acceptance_criteria.rationale: Reviewers need to see an application's screens at catalog scale and reach the behavior each one shows without committed images.

scenarios.given: a catalog of about a thousand screens
scenarios.then: every screen must fit in the window on one board, without requesting an image until cards are large enough to see
scenarios.when: the reviewer switches the Screens view to the canvas

acceptance_criteria.criterion: The review page must highlight the Stories, Acceptance Criteria, and screens a branch added, changed, or removed relative to a base ref, including screens whose screenshot was re-captured, using only git and keeping every record navigable.
acceptance_criteria.rationale: Reviewers of a pull request need to see which behavior and which screens moved without a database, a hosted service, or committed screenshots.

scenarios.given: a branch re-captures a screenshot without changing the screen's catalog fields
scenarios.then: the screen must be reported as changed because its recorded image digest differs
scenarios.when: the screens are imported and the review page is rendered against the base ref

scenarios.given: the base ref has no compiled manifest
scenarios.then: every record must be reported as new and the page must say why
scenarios.when: the review page is rendered against it

scenarios.given: a branch re-captures a screen whose committed ARIA snapshot changed
scenarios.then: the screen must be reported as changed with a text aspect, apart from its image and catalog fields
scenarios.when: the review page is rendered against the base ref

scenarios.given: a branch removes an acceptance criterion from a Story
scenarios.then: the criterion must stay at the end of that Story, struck through and marked removed, and the Story's header must say it changed
scenarios.when: the review page is rendered against the base ref

scenarios.given: a reviewer wants only what the branch changed
scenarios.then: the navigation must list only changed Stories, or the map only new and changed screens, and pressing it again must restore the rest
scenarios.when: they press Changed in the Stories or Screens view

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Tieline must report screens missing a screenshot digest, a capture record, a committed ARIA snapshot, or a literal @screen test tag, ARIA snapshots that differ from their capture record or belong to no catalogued screen, and screens captured in different environments, through screens audit and as check warnings that never change the check's exit code, reading test files and snapshots only within fixed bounds and never through symbolic links.
acceptance_criteria.rationale: Incremental capture only re-captures screens a branch may affect, so a cheap audit must find what it cannot, and check must surface it without making an unrelated pull request fail.

scenarios.given: the tag scan stops at one of its bounds
scenarios.then: screens must not be reported as missing a test, and the audit must say why the scan is incomplete

scenarios.given: a capture record's ARIA snapshot digest differs from the committed snapshot
scenarios.then: Tieline must warn about the mismatch and keep the exit code the check would otherwise have

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Tieline must select the screens a branch may have changed since its branch point, because their committed capture outputs or catalog entry changed, a changed test tags them, a Story or AC that shows them links a changed file, a changed file or one of its code-topology dependents matches their paths or their showing Stories' and ACs' links, or a configured global path changed, and must report every reason for each screen and every rule it could not evaluate.
acceptance_criteria.rationale: Re-capturing only affected screens keeps pull requests fast, and selection is a heuristic, so reviewers must see why each screen was chosen and where the selection may be narrower than it should be.

scenarios.given: a branch changes a shared component and the code topology is stale
scenarios.then: Tieline must report the dependency rule as unavailable rather than select nothing silently
scenarios.when: screens changed since the base are selected

scenarios.given: a branch changes a screen's committed screenshot digest by hand
scenarios.then: the screen must be selected so that verification re-captures it
scenarios.when: screens changed since the base are selected

scenarios.given: a branch removes or renames a test's @screen tag, or renames the test out of a test file name, and nothing else selects that screen
scenarios.then: the screen must be selected, from the tags the test had at the branch point
scenarios.when: the screens it may have changed are selected

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Tieline must capture selected screens with the repository's own Playwright tests tagged @screen:<key>, must write screenshots, committed ARIA snapshots, and capture records only when every selected screen was captured exactly once by a passing test, must bound, validate, and re-hash everything the run produces, must stop a run at its timeout or on cancellation without writing, and with verify must change no committed output, keeping only screenshots it reproduced exactly in the git-ignored captures directory and only when hosted screens are enabled, and must fail when a selected screen's committed outputs differ from a fresh capture, verifying every screen instead of a branch's changed ones when a selection rule could not run.
acceptance_criteria.rationale: Committed screen outputs are reviewed as the truth about how screens look, so a partial, untrusted, or stale capture must never replace them, and pull requests must not merge with outputs a fresh capture would not reproduce.

scenarios.given: one selected screen's test fails or captures nothing
scenarios.then: Tieline must name the screen and the failure and write no catalog, snapshot, or screenshot

scenarios.given: a committed screenshot digest was captured in a different environment
scenarios.then: Tieline must report the environment difference rather than compare the digests

scenarios.given: a test calls tielineSnapshot for a key it is not tagged with
scenarios.then: the test must fail and say which tag to add
scenarios.when: the test runs, inside or outside a capture run

scenarios.given: the catalog cannot be written after the capture replaced screenshots and ARIA snapshots
scenarios.then: every screenshot and ARIA snapshot it replaced must be restored, so the catalog's digests and the captures directory still agree

scenarios.given: a capture that runs in several batches or is repeated
scenarios.then: it must stop without writing, the limit covering every batch and repeat together

scenarios.given: a capture that runs in several batches or is repeated
scenarios.then: the screenshots and ARIA snapshots it keeps must each stay within one byte bound across every batch, and a repeat run must keep only the digests it is compared by

stories.benefit: UI states and copy are reviewed with the behavior and code they belong to
stories.goal: catalog an application's user-visible screens beside the Stories and Acceptance Criteria they show
stories.title: Review the screens that show accepted behavior
